why: a regular expression literal in a call is a bodiless function of the literal's text and its operands (heap-stage5.md section 6), and the named captures of a match of a non-global literal bound to a const are one more function of the pattern and the string: isCode tests the same literal on a renamed string and compares with true (proved); tidy replaces the same global pattern by another replacement (unproved, WITNESS); year reads the same named capture through the optional chain with a default, as the match is absent or not (proved); month reads another named capture of the same match (unproved, WITNESS). second reads a numbered capture of a group that may not take part, undefined when the other alternative matches, with another default (unproved, WITNESS on "a"); first reads a numbered capture of a group in every match (proved); day destructures the named captures (proved); keyed reads a named capture by a literal key (proved); held matches a pattern held in a module const bound to a literal (proved); either reads a named group of one alternative, absent when the other matches, with another default (unproved, WITNESS). tested matches a string the unit tests with `!` before the match, which is no write (proved).
